measured.swap: conformance PASSED 13/13 before (dryrun, local-signed-jsonl) and 13/13 after (second, keyless-transparency-log) with the same 13 cases; sha256 of interface.py+call.py+conformance.py identical across both runs (7fbc16d2e67dd4e2c093401ae5b475b4307c11e6e7cd03d002c0d551610a8792), so the swap was configuration; 7 execution-model axes differ (signer authority possession vs expiring-identity, key lifetime long-lived vs per-run discarded, store hash-chained jsonl vs append-only merkle log, verifying material out-of-band vs published with the envelope, offline capable true vs false, inclusion proofs declared unsupported vs 1 verified, store integrity chain recompute vs log-root recompute); both reports carry store_mounted=false, external_verifier_exit=0, attestations_verified>0, subject_mismatches=0, orphan_subjects=0, selected_by=configuration, merged adapters_run=2; the same caller code ran unchanged on both and the log binding returned an inclusion proof the caller never asked for.
measured.breakage: two, both fail. (1) the definition-of-done breakage: the artifact is rebuilt from a modified input and the attestation is left alone (conformance.py --break rebuilt-artifact); the run exits 1 with subject_mismatches=1, attestations_verified=0 and the store-unmounted verifier exiting 1 on the subject digest, not on our store. (2) the signature is dropped from the envelope (--break dropped-signature) on the second adapter; the run exits 1 and names 'the envelope carries no signature'. The green checks in steps 1 and 2 can therefore fail.

Today's component for this capability is a local store, so no endpoint was involved.
measured.coverage: bash harness/provenance/test.sh step 6 (coverage.py, gated: previously named in no gate) on 2026-09-04: coverage.py is invoked twice for one period with no reset between the two process invocations, and the manifest grows from 2 to 4 entries -- not truncated between runs (concern-provenance-q3's second finding). reconcile() enumerates the artifact store's directory (ground truth: os.listdir, not a self-reported log) against manifest entries with a resolvable attestation; two deliberate breakages exercise the two enforcement layers the closure names: --break bypass-refused calls the manifest's only write path with no attestation and it raises document-invalid before anything is appended (refused at write time, not counted after the fact); --break filesystem-escape writes a file straight into the artifact store's directory, the one route the write-time refusal cannot reach because it does not own the filesystem, and reconcile()/admission_check() catch it anyway by enumeration, exiting non-zero and naming the unattested artifact_id. emit.py factors the boundary (attest_and_record) out of coverage.py so it is the same function, not a look-alike, that examples/end-to-end/run.py's Run.call_agent() and harness/linked/linked.py's Linked._run() call at their own real production boundaries (grep -c attest run.py: 4; grep -c 'attest|provenance' linked.py: 7, both previously 0) -- both harnesses' own test.sh remain green with the wiring in place.

claimed: verification by a tool we did not write: no third-party verifier is available in this environment, so external_verifier names this repository's own conformance.py run as a separate process. What is measured is that verification reads only the envelope, the trust policy and the digest the holder computed, with our store unreachable and no adapter imported; that it would also satisfy a foreign verifier is claimed (F-b4-05, X-cap-provenance-005)

public verifiability: hmac-sha256 over the DSSE pre-authentication encoding stands in for a signature, because only hashlib and hmac are available here, so the verifying material is the signing key and a holder of it could also sign. The envelope, the PAE, the subject binding, the inclusion proof and the swap are real; replacing mac() in interface.py with an asymmetric signer changes nothing else in the file

the standards' versions: in-toto Statement v1, SLSA v1.1-or-v1.0 and DSSE are unverified, every record on file for them being a search result rather than a fetched page (STATUS row 45, absent-by-owner on the standard stick). The DSSE PAE spelling and the log's audit-path format are unverified for the same reason
the predicate type URIs are this platform's own and are proposed: no fetched record on file carries a predicate type URI for a build or for an agent action (cap-provenance instruction 4)
the networked form of the second adapter until TRANSPARENCY_LOG_URL and IDENTITY_URL point at real routes; the dry run exercises its identity, log, proof and refusal-to-sign-offline in process
SLSA level: no build-track level is claimed here at all (X-build-definition-of-done-007); this harness signs a statement, it does not assert a hardened build platform
monitoring the log: store_integrity() recomputes the root over every entry when asked, which is a check on demand and not a monitor anybody runs (X-cross-structure-053, cap-provenance step 7)
